p1c10.caption: the skirmish rank, centre plate struck
p1c10.opener: #chapter-art.motif emblem (skirmish-gallery, 340px: three upright shield-plates in rank, outer bone, centre bronze split crown-to-foot by the ember crack from the crown strike-diamond; 10 bone rings) + DM Sans caption; then .chapter-meta at FULL book title scale (long discursive chapter, Cinzel percent rule). The opener shows one plate already hit — the raids that follow are the hammer working down the rank.
p1c10.palette_role: Full grammar at campaign weight: bone rank, bronze centre plate, ember crack + spurs. 10 rings (T1) — the densest circular set in the book; only p1c12's collapse tops it.
p1c10.part_subtitle: How to Philosophize with a Hammer
p1c10.rationale: The longest chapter (61 served paras) is a gallery of sounded targets, opened by the muster-roll 'My Impossibles' ('Seneca: or the toreador of virtue … Kant: or cant … Victor Hugo: or the pharos by the sea of nonsense') and closed by the valediction 'I have given humanity the most profound book it possesses, my Zarathustra: I shall shortly give it the most independent one.' Between them the hammer falls on writers (Sainte-Beuve, G. Eliot, Sand, Emerson), psychologists ('to the psychologist a case of the first order', the 'evil eye', the 'impersonal' type), art itself ('L'art pour l'art means: the devil take morality!', Apollonian/Dionysian intoxication), and modern institutions ('the herd animal triumphs', 'democratism has always been the form taken by organizing energy in decline'). The rank-of-shields emblem literalizes the raid logic: every target gets one strike; the centre plate shows what a landed strike looks like.
p1c10.reading_treatment: Calm Cormorant body, book drop-cap kept (raid 01 label floats above the cap line per R1 micro-note). 22 raid starts (prototype RAIDS indices verbatim) carry family pips via p.raid-start[data-raid]::before with data-URI content (source anchors dusk-raid-*-view): pen = literary raids 2/3/4/7, eye = psychology raids 5/8/9/11/14/17/18, mask = art raid 10, sword = politics raids 12/15/20/21; dusk-raid-major-view movement heads at raids 1/6/13/16/19/22. Book 'raid NN' ::after labels kept, re-offset for pip width. Final graf (idx 60, the Zarathustra valediction) as right-aligned italic ash signature close. Cohort dusk-seal end-mark (28px).
p1c10.title: Reconnaissance Raids of an Untimely Man

p1c11.caption: Dionysos wreathed, at noon
p1c11.opener: #chapter-art.motif emblem (dionysian-mask, min(360px,78vw): bronze applique mask of Dionysos — hooded lids, articulated pupils, open mouth, ivy-leaf wreath with ember corymbs — centred on the noon sun-disc with 4 bronze cardinal ray ticks; ember brow crack from the crown strike-diamond; 11 bone rings) + DM Sans caption; then .chapter-meta at full book title scale. The mask faces the reader: this chapter is an approach ('a word about the world which I sought to approach'), not a demolition.
p1c11.palette_role: Bronze-dominant: noon disc, wreath, rays. Ember confined to the brow crack + 3 corymb dots — the wound that sanctifies. 11 rings (T1), the fullest circular count before the verdict.
p1c11.part_subtitle: How to Philosophize with a Hammer
p1c11.rationale: Anchored end to end in the 7 served paras: Roman style learned from Sallust ('Terse, austere … a cool malice towards the fine phrase') and Horace ('This mosaic of words … noble par excellence'); 'Plato is boring' and the 'superior swindle' of idealism versus Thucydides ('Thucydides has himself under control, therefore he keeps things, too, under his control'); the Greeks' will to power behind their institutions; then the turn — 'I was the first person who … took seriously that marvellous phenomenon which bears the name of Dionysus' — through the Lobeck demolition to the sanctified close: 'the torment of the woman in labour must also exist eternally', 'the eternal joy of becoming', 'I, the last disciple of the philosopher Dionysus'. The wreathed mask on the noon disc is that final paragraph made emblem: noon light, orgiastic excess, the crack across the brow where the hammer tested even joy. Cardinal rays are class arc-deco, never counted (T1).
p1c11.reading_treatment: 7 long grafs, calm body, book drop-cap. The aphoristic core — para idx 2 ('Thucydides and Plato: Plato is a coward in the face of reality …') — is set as a centred verdict stone (max 54ch, 2.4em air above/below): the chapter's kill line given room. Closing graf (idx 6, Dionysus/eternal recurrence) gets 2.2em top air. Cohort dusk-seal end-mark (28px).
p1c11.title: What I Owe The Ancients

p1c12.caption: the diamond over the coal
p1c12.opener: POSTER (T4 + Cinzel percent rule): airy verdict opener — diamond-over-coal emblem at min(340px,76vw) above a SMALL Cinzel title (book.css 600/small-clamp/wide-tracking rule already in place — do not fight it), generous top air (padding-top 2.5rem). The emblem: bronze faceted diamond over the ash coal-lump, 2.0px ember verdict crack through gem into coal, ember strike-point at the crown; 6 outer bone circles + 6 collapsing bone diamonds (class 'ring diamond') = 12 (T1 '12→diamond'). Explicit end state below (reading_treatment) so the 8-verse chapter reads finished.
p1c12.palette_role: Brightest bone + bronze in the cohort against the ember bed: the verdict gem. 12 collapsing into diamond (T1) — the sounding sequence resolves; no chapter after this one.
p1c12.part_subtitle: How to Philosophize with a Hammer
p1c12.rationale: Every gesture quotes the 8 served verses: the coal's question ('Why so hard! … for are we not close kin?') answered by the hammer's counter-question ('Why so soft? Oh my brethren'); hardness that must 'flash and cut and cleave' to join in creating; 'Bliss to write upon the will of millennia as upon bronze — harder than bronze, nobler than bronze'; and the closing table 'become hard!'. The emblem stages the kinship (one ash lump, one bronze gem, same ground) and the verdict (the ember crack that does not shatter the diamond but proves it).
p1c12.reading_treatment: POSTER end-state (T4): no drop-cap — P1 '(Thus Spake Zarathustra, III)' is an attribution line, set small centred ash. Verses (idx 1–7) centred, max 56ch, airy. The bronze verse (idx 6, 'Bliss to write upon the will of millennia as upon bronze') is the bronze inscription close: centred, bronze first line. The final verse (idx 7, 'become hard!') is the verdict line: centred, bone, +0.06em letterspacing, 1.15em — Cormorant, never Cinzel body (percent rule). Cohort dusk-seal end-mark (28px) below.
p1c12.title: The Hammer Speaks

p1c9.caption: the dancing quill strikes the flatland
p1c9.opener: #chapter-art.motif emblem (dancing-pen, 300px: bronze quill dancing back from the strike-point diamond on the flatland horizon line, ember hairline crack descending; 9 bone rings: 7 fine + 2 hero) + DM Sans caption; then .chapter-meta at full book title scale (long discursive chapter). Lightest emblem in the cohort — thinnest strokes, widest arcs, smallest ember — because this chapter diagnoses heaviness and prescribes lightness.
p1c9.palette_role: Bronze pen-work on ash ground; ember only the 1px descent crack. 9 rings (T1) — the closing movement opens mid-crescendo.
p1c9.part_subtitle: How to Philosophize with a Hammer
p1c9.rationale: Anchored in the 10 served paras: the inherited moderation 'more in need of the goad than the brake shoe'; Germany seen 'more and more as Europe's flatland' (the emblem's bronze horizon line); the three tasks — 'You have to learn to see, you have to learn to think, you have to learn to speak and write' — with thinking learned 'just as dancing needs to be learned, as a kind of dancing'; and the finale 'the ability to dance with the feet, with concepts, with words … you must also be able to dance with the pen — that you must learn to write?' The quill dancing back from its own impact is that last sentence: the pen that learned to dance.
p1c9.reading_treatment: Calm body, book drop-cap kept. Honest narrow dancing-baseline: the yea-saying turn (idx 7, 'In order not to be untrue to my type, which is yea-saying …') gets 2.6em top air + a small bronze arc divider (p::before data-URI, curves never rails) marking diagnosis→prescription; the finale (idx 9, dance with the pen) is centred with a bronze first line (the dancing clause). No per-line stagger — the served text has no verse lines to stagger, and faking them would lie. Cohort dusk-seal end-mark (28px).
p1c9.title: What The Germans Lack

direction_comparison.name: D1. Funereal dusk (rejected)
direction_comparison.note: Low crepuscular washes, violet-black gradients, sinking setting-sun disc per opener. Rejected: gradients-as-subject are banned by the R1 verdict (Q1 — line-work must lead, washes stay subservient); literal dusk scenery repeats the rejected baseline's bronze-band mood instead of the approved sounding procedure; a setting sun misreads the book's arc, which ends at verdict-noon ('become hard'), not nightfall.

direction_comparison.name: D2. Marble noon (rejected)
direction_comparison.note: Pale stone grounds, chiselled inscription panels, flat gold noon mass behind p1c11/p1c12. Rejected: flat gold mural mass belongs to Gay Science (T5 separation — Twilight noon is engraved bronze line, never mass); white marble grounds break the dark-first forge identity; cold classicism misreads the polemic's heat (ember cracks, 'the devil take morality', cheerfulness as method).

direction_comparison.name: D3. Ring-density crescendo + bronze inscription (CHOSEN — inside the approved grammar)
direction_comparison.note: No new identity: the cohort plays the book's chosen STRUCK BRONZE grammar at closing-movement pressure. Compositional engine = the T1 ring counts themselves: 9→10→11→collapse, emblems growing and ember deepening across the four openers while the reading body stays calm. p1c10's gallery logic gets the four-family pip system (pen/eye/mask/sword + major heads); p1c12 resolves to poster (whisper Cinzel already in book.css + bronze inscription verse + dusk seal). Kept from art-direction: palette, Cinzel/Cormorant/DM Sans roles, strike-point signature, percent rule, T1–T6. Added (cohort-local, nothing book-level): crescendo sizing, family pips, dusk-seal end-mark, p1c9 narrow dancing-baseline, p1c11 verdict stone. Title-swap test: rings-counting quills, a cracked skirmish rank, a wreathed noon mask and a diamond-over-coal verdict read wrong on any other book.

1.justification: Title 'My Impossibles' opens the muster-roll of writers judged as stylists — Rousseau, Schiller, Hugo ('the pharos by the sea of nonsense'), Sand ('the milk cow with beautiful style'), Zola. The pen sounds first.
1.pip: dusk-raid-major-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
1.title: My Impossibles

10.justification: Title is the art-slogan itself; the served head reads 'L'artpour I'art' (typesetting artifact — body repeats 'L'art pour l'art means: the devil take morality!'). Art judging art: the mask.
10.pip: dusk-raid-mask-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
10.title: L'art pour l'art

11.justification: A character study of the 'impersonal' type's self-deception ('Getting personal — the virtue of the impersonal') — the eye reading a soul, not a book.
11.pip: dusk-raid-eye-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
11.title: The ‘impersonal’ have a chance to speak

12.justification: The viva catechism indicts the state schooling machine ('To turn man into a machine … Who is the perfect human being? The public servant') — an institution, hence the sword.
12.pip: dusk-raid-sword-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
12.title: From a Doctoral Viva

13.justification: Title 'Another Problem of Diet' prescribes a physiology of genius — Caesar's marches protecting 'that subtle machine … called genius'. The eye's clinical material; movement head.
13.pip: dusk-raid-major-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
13.title: Another Problem of Diet

14.justification: Title judges selfishness by 'physiological value' (ascendant vs descendent line of life) — a clinical reading of character.
14.pip: dusk-raid-eye-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
14.title: Natural Value of Egoism

15.justification: Title pairs the anarchist with the Christian as decadents; the raid's logic is revolution ('this is the logic on which revolutions are based') — the sword.
15.pip: dusk-raid-sword-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
15.title: Christian and Anarchist

16.justification: Served title 'Critique of Décadence Morality' diagnoses altruism as physiology ('a physiological one: I can't find my own advantage any more … Disgregation of the instincts!'). The eye's clinic; movement head.
16.pip: dusk-raid-major-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
16.title: Critique of Décadence Morality

17.justification: Title addresses physicians; the raid prescribes disgust-doses, free death, and reads pessimism as cholera statistics — medicine as psychology.
17.pip: dusk-raid-eye-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
17.title: Morality for Physicians

18.justification: Title asks after our moral self-image; the raid contrasts Renaissance fullness with modern 'old wives' morality' and the 'pathos of distance' — moral psychology, not statecraft.
18.pip: dusk-raid-eye-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
18.title: Whether We Have Become More Moral

19.justification: Title 'My Idea of Freedom' attacks liberal institutions ('herd-animalization'), weighs war, tyrants, and nations (Rome, Venice, Caesar) — statecraft throughout. Movement head.
19.pip: dusk-raid-major-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
19.title: My Idea of Freedom

2.justification: Title names the French literary critic; the raid judges him as critic and historian ('As a critic lacking a yardstick … As a historian lacking a philosophy'). The pen answers the pen.
2.pip: dusk-raid-pen-view (source anchor; ships as CSS data-URI)
2.title: Sainte-Beuve

20.justification: Title indicts modern institutions — democracy, the 'German Reich', authority, marriage, the labour question ('people think they are in danger of a new form of slavery'). The sword.
